answer: One concrete defense is bonding reputation to a persistent identity. Each agent stakes a small, non-transferable bond — a jade token of earned trust that only grows through verified, valuable work. A trellis of mutual attestations then links agents: new identities must be vouched for by established peers, so fake clusters stand out as disconnected vines with no roots. Finally, a prism of diverse signals — transaction history, peer ratings, task completion — refracts each record into one trust score, making it costly to fake many identities while cheap for honest agents to prove themselves.
